status: DRAFT — review with the cyber team before replacing data/mock/questions.mock.json
notes: IDs are NIST CSF 2.0 subcategories. Extra fields (cisSafeguards, cisIg, difficulty, critical) are used by the scoring rules and the synthetic data generator; the web app ignores them. 20 questions; quick set = 10 (one or more per function).

questions.text: Does your organization have a written information security policy that management has approved and staff can access?
questions.description: Partially = a policy exists but is outdated (older than 2 years) or not shared with staff.

questions.text: Is a specific person or team named as responsible for cybersecurity, with time and authority to do the job?
questions.description: Partially = someone handles security informally, on top of another job, with no clear authority.

questions.text: Do you check the security of suppliers and IT service providers that can access your systems or data?
questions.description: Partially = only for some suppliers, or only when the contract is signed.

questions.text: Do you keep an up-to-date inventory of all computers, servers and network devices?
questions.description: Partially = an inventory exists but is incomplete or not updated in the last 6 months.

questions.text: Do you keep an up-to-date list of the software and cloud services your organization uses?
questions.description: Partially = a list exists but is incomplete or not updated in the last 6 months.

questions.text: Do you know where your important and personal data is stored and who can access it (for example a PDPA record of processing)?
questions.description: Partially = known for some systems only, or not written down.

questions.text: Do you regularly scan your systems for vulnerabilities and record what you find?
questions.description: Partially = scans happen only occasionally (less than once a quarter) or results are not tracked.

questions.text: Is multi-factor authentication (MFA) required for email, remote access and admin accounts?
questions.description: Partially = MFA is used for some of these but not all.

questions.text: Do staff only get the access they need for their job, with admin rights limited and access reviewed regularly?
questions.description: Partially = access is limited but never reviewed, or many users have admin rights.

questions.text: Do all staff receive security awareness training (for example phishing training) at least once a year?
questions.description: Partially = only some staff, or only at onboarding.

questions.text: Is sensitive data encrypted on laptops, servers and in cloud storage?
questions.description: Partially = encrypted on some devices or storage only.

questions.text: Are backups of important data made automatically, kept separate from the main network, and test-restored?
questions.description: Partially = backups exist but are never test-restored, or are stored on the same network.

questions.text: Is your network protected by a firewall, with important systems separated from staff and guest Wi-Fi?
questions.description: Partially = a firewall exists but the network is not separated, or rules are never reviewed.

questions.text: Are security updates for operating systems and applications installed within a set time (for example 30 days)?
questions.description: Partially = updates are installed, but with no set timeline or not on all systems.

questions.text: Is installing or running unapproved software blocked on company computers?
questions.description: Partially = staff are told not to, but it is not technically blocked.

questions.text: Are network activity and security logs collected centrally and reviewed for suspicious events?
questions.description: Partially = logs are collected but rarely reviewed, or only on some systems.

questions.text: Do all computers and servers run up-to-date anti-malware or endpoint protection (EDR) that alerts someone?
questions.description: Partially = installed on some devices, or alerts are not checked.

questions.text: Do you know who must be told about a security incident and how fast (for example, PDPA requires notifying the regulator within 72 hours of a personal data breach)?
questions.description: Partially = some contacts are known but there is no written list or timeline.

questions.text: Do you have a written incident response plan that says who does what when a security incident happens?
questions.description: Partially = the plan exists but has never been tested or reviewed.

questions.text: Do you have a tested plan to restore critical systems, with target recovery times?
questions.description: Partially = a recovery plan exists but has no recovery time targets or has not been tested.
